constraints.translation: The Agreement is entered into between the two parties.
constraints.reasoning: Directly stated as the agreement’s formation clause.

constraints.translation: Each is a “Party”, and together they are the “Parties”.
The Parties wish to explore possible co-operation.
constraints.reasoning: Stated intent using “wish” (strongly asserted intent, but not a strict obligation).

constraints.translation: If they explore the co-operation, then they wish to explore it.
constraints.reasoning: Exploring tends to align with wishing to explore, but it is not logically necessary.

constraints.translation: The Parties may disclose essential confidential information during evaluations/discussions/negotiations.
constraints.reasoning: Use of “may” indicates permission/possibility rather than certainty.

constraints.translation: Confidential information is an essential part of the Disclosing Party’s operations.
Unauthorised disclosure will damage the Disclosing Party’s competitive situation.
constraints.reasoning: Explicit “will” prediction; near-certain within the document’s rationale.

constraints.translation: Disclosure and use shall be on the terms of this Agreement.
Definition of Confidential Information includes business/research/product/service info, the agreement terms, and discussion/oral presentation info.
Specified categories are excluded from Confidential Information.
constraints.reasoning: Explicit exclusions stated as “shall not include”.

constraints.translation: The Agreement will not restrict compliance with lawful disclosure orders/requirements.
Receiving Party will promptly notify the Disclosing Party upon learning of such order/requirement.
constraints.reasoning: Stated as a condition (“provided, however, that … will promptly notify”).

constraints.translation: The Parties shall only use Confidential Information for negotiation/evaluation of co-operation.
The Parties shall not disclose Confidential Information to third parties without prior written approval.
Disclosure to officers/employees/consultants on a need-to-know basis is allowed without prior written approval.
constraints.evidence: 2.4 exception: “other than to their officers, employees or consultants … on a need to know basis”
constraints.reasoning: Text explicitly carves out an exception; treated as strong permission.

constraints.translation: Each Party shall ensure internal recipients are bound by confidentiality undertakings at least as protective as this Agreement.
All disclosed Confidential Information remains the Disclosing Party’s property.
Receiving Party shall not be entitled to copy Confidential Information except as necessary.
On request or on termination, Receiving Party must return/delete/destroy Confidential Information as instructed.
constraints.reasoning: Both triggering conditions are explicitly stated with “shall”.

constraints.translation: Receiving Party shall certify in writing and confirm no copies retained.
Confidential Information remains Disclosing Party’s exclusive property and no rights/licenses are granted to Receiving Party.
For each material breach, Receiving Party shall pay liquidated damages of SEK [amount] per breach.
constraints.reasoning: Stated with “shall”, but the section notes it is only applicable in some agreements.

constraints.translation: Disclosing Party may pursue other legal measures and claim damages exceeding liquidated damages.
constraints.reasoning: Explicit rights stated as present (“has the right”).

constraints.translation: Agreement term is one year when signed.
Confidentiality obligations continue for five years after termination.
Provisions apply retroactively to Confidential Information disclosed prior to the effective date in connection with the co-operation discussions.
Neither Party may assign without the other’s prior written consent.
Governing law is Sweden.
Disputes are exclusively settled by the District Court of [city] as first instance.
constraints.reasoning: Presented as the primary clause, but an explicit bracketed alternative arbitration clause suggests a template choice.

constraints.translation: Disputes are finally settled by arbitration under SCC Expedited Arbitration Rules (alternative clause).
constraints.reasoning: Bracketed optional text indicates it may be substituted; weaker commitment in the template as provided.

constraints.translation: Agreement executed in two copies; each party takes one.
“Shall only use …” corresponds to “only use …” (de-modalized version).
constraints.reasoning: The paired propositions represent the same contractual content with/without the modal word.

constraints.translation: “Shall not disclose …” corresponds to “do not disclose …” (de-modalized version).
constraints.reasoning: The paired propositions represent the same contractual restriction with/without the modal word.

constraints.translation: “Shall ensure …” corresponds to “ensures …” (de-modalized version).
“Shall remain the property …” corresponds to “remains the property …”.
Copy entitlement restriction with/without “shall”.
Return/delete/destroy upon request with/without “shall”.
Return/delete/destroy upon termination with/without “shall”.
Certification requirement with/without “shall”.
Liquidated damages liability with/without “shall”.
Agreement term with/without “shall”.
Confidentiality survival period with/without “shall”.
Retroactivity with/without “shall”.
Assignment restriction with/without “shall”.
Governing law clause with/without “shall”.
If Swedish law governs, then it is not governed by Norway/England & Wales/US law.
